title: r/soapmaking
tagline: Soap and skincare makers with frequent where-to-buy threads.
audience: Cold-process devotees, melt-and-pour beginners, and skincare-curious lurkers. The "where do you buy handmade soap" threads that pop up here are shopping lists waiting for names.
overview:
A craft-first community where cut videos and swirl techniques get the applause. Cold-process makers dominate the conversation, trading lye-safety wisdom and recipe math, while melt-and-pour beginners arrive daily asking where to start.

What makes it commercially interesting is its lurker base: because everyone uses soap, the audience skews more buyer-curious than most maker subreddits. The recurring recommendation threads are genuine purchase moments, and the names that appear in them belong to makers the community already trusts.
discussions:
Cut videos and swirl reveals — the community's signature content
Recipe formulation: oils, superfat percentages, lye calculators
Curing setups, storage, and how long is long enough
Scent blending: what survives saponification and what vanishes
Labeling laws and what you can legally claim on skin products
loves:
Satisfying cut videos — the format that travels far beyond the subreddit
Recipe generosity; sharing a base recipe costs nothing, execution is the product
Real knowledge about skin sensitivities and ingredient behavior
dislikes:
Health claims that overreach — this community knows the FDA line
Drama about "stolen" recipes; technique is considered shared culture
Drive-by promotion with no participation
rules:
Self-promotion is restricted to what subreddit rules allow — check before posting anything shop-adjacent
Medical or therapeutic claims about products are both against the rules and legally risky
Safety-first culture: skipping lye safety in tutorials gets posts removed
approach: Show your cuts and cure racks, answer scent and sensitivity questions with real knowledge, and be generous with base recipes. The trust that builds is what gets your name dropped when the buying threads appear.

title: r/SkincareAddiction
tagline: Millions of ingredient-literate buyers who will read your label properly.
audience: Skincare obsessives who know their actives, read INCI lists and distrust marketing. Demanding, but they spend heavily and recommend relentlessly when convinced.
overview:
The largest skincare community anywhere and among the most rigorous. Members evaluate products on formulation rather than branding, and they will notice if a claim doesn't hold up.

That rigour is an opportunity for small makers who are honest: this audience actively prefers a modest, well-explained product over a hyped one.
discussions:
Routine help and product recommendation requests
Ingredient science — actives, percentages, incompatibilities
Brand critiques, often unsparing
Before-and-after progress posts
Sensitive-skin and reaction troubleshooting
loves:
Full ingredient transparency and realistic claims
Products that don't overpromise
Makers who explain formulation honestly, including limitations
dislikes:
Unsupported claims, especially medical ones
Undisclosed marketing or shill accounts
"Natural" used as a substitute for evidence
rules:
Strict anti-self-promotion enforcement; undisclosed marketing gets banned
Medical claims are removed
Affiliation must be disclosed if you comment about your own product
approach: Do not promote here — genuinely, it will backfire. Use it to learn what informed buyers actually ask, then answer those questions on your own product pages before anyone has to ask.
tags: skincare, beauty, serum, ingredients, sensitive skin, cosmetics

title: r/IndieMakeupAndMore
tagline: A community built specifically to find and buy from small beauty brands.
audience: Indie beauty enthusiasts who actively seek out tiny makers — perfume oils, small-batch cosmetics, artisan bath products. They want to find you.
overview:
Unusually welcoming for a beauty community, because its entire purpose is discovering brands too small to advertise. Members trade samples, review indie releases and ask constantly for recommendations in specific niches.

This is the rare room where being a one-person operation is an advantage rather than a credibility problem.
discussions:
Indie brand recommendations by scent or product type
Sample swaps and decant trading
New release announcements and first impressions
Restock alerts for small-batch drops
Honest reviews, including the unflattering ones
loves:
Genuinely distinctive products they can't get elsewhere
Small makers who engage as people
Detailed scent and texture descriptions
dislikes:
Large brands positioning as indie
Undisclosed brand accounts
Hype without substance
rules:
Brand participation usually requires disclosure and often mod approval
Self-promotion rules are specific — read them before posting anything
Reviews must disclose if products were gifted
approach: Read the rules on brand participation carefully, then follow them exactly. Where brand accounts are permitted with disclosure, this community will genuinely champion a small maker who shows up honestly.
tags: indie beauty, perfume, cosmetics, bath, skincare, small batch, fragrance

title: r/fragrance
tagline: Serious scent people who buy samples endlessly and talk about nothing else.
audience: Fragrance collectors ranging from casual to deeply obsessive. They own dozens of bottles, buy samples constantly, and are always hunting the next discovery.
overview:
A large and knowledgeable community organised entirely around scent. Members discuss notes, longevity and projection with a precision that borders on wine criticism, and indie houses are actively sought out.

Sample culture is strong here, which is perfect for a small perfumer — the barrier to trying you is a few dollars rather than a full bottle.
discussions:
Scent-of-the-day threads, daily and busy
Note breakdowns and dupe hunting
Longevity and projection debates
Sample and decant recommendations
Indie and niche house discoveries
loves:
Detailed, honest scent descriptions using real vocabulary
Sample availability — nobody buys a full bottle blind
Indie perfumers who talk about their materials
dislikes:
Marketing language instead of actual scent description
Undisclosed brand promotion
Overclaiming longevity, which they will test and report
rules:
Self-promotion requires disclosure and is often restricted
Reviews must disclose gifted or free products
Dupe discussions have limits around trademark and counterfeits
approach: Offer samples cheaply and describe your scents in the community's own vocabulary — top, heart, base, longevity. This audience never buys blind, so make trying you almost free and let the reviews do the rest.
tags: fragrance, perfume, scent, oil, cologne, indie

title: #SoapCutting
tagline: Billions of views of soap being sliced — the purest ASMR product content there is.
audience: An enormous audience watching for satisfaction rather than shopping. Small conversion rate, colossal numbers — and the ones who do convert become regulars.
overview:
One of the earliest and largest satisfying-content categories on the platform. A soap loaf being cut needs no explanation, no music and no face on camera, and it reliably holds attention.

The commercial mechanic is patience: the audience arrives for the sound, stays for the colours, and eventually asks where to buy.
discussions:
Loaf cutting in close-up with natural sound
Swirl and layer reveals
Embed and design experiments
Cure-rack and batch-day content
Restock announcements to an already-large audience
loves:
Crisp sound and clean cuts, close to the camera
Unusual swirls and colour combinations
Consistent posting, which compounds fast here
dislikes:
Music drowning out the cutting sound, which is the point
Stolen footage, common in this category and quickly called out
Bait content that isn't actually soap
rules:
Commercial music licensing applies
Re-uploading others' cutting videos is rampant and heavily reported
Shop features require commerce eligibility
approach: Film every single cut day with natural sound and no music. The audience builds slowly then very fast — and because they came for the process, they trust the product when you finally mention it.
tags: soap, soap making, bath, asmr, cold process, handmade

title: #naturalskincare
tagline: Buyers actively avoiding big-brand formulations and looking for small makers.
audience: People who read ingredient lists and prefer short ones. Often sensitive-skin sufferers who've had bad experiences with mainstream products and will stay loyal once something works.
overview:
A discovery tag for small-batch and botanical skincare. The aesthetic is consistent — natural light, raw ingredients in frame, muted packaging — and posts that fit it get engagement well above their follower count.

The audience's defining trait is caution, which means education outperforms promotion by a wide margin.
discussions:
Ingredient spotlights and what each one does
Routine and layering guidance
Before-and-after for sensitive or reactive skin
Batch-making and studio process
Packaging and sustainability choices
loves:
Raw ingredients shown alongside the finished product
Educational captions that teach rather than sell
Honest limits — saying what a product won't do
dislikes:
Vague natural claims with no specifics
Medical-sounding promises
Overstyled shots that hide what's actually in the jar
rules:
Cosmetic claim regulations apply to what you can say on a public post
Algorithmic relevance applies to tagging
Before-and-after imagery is scrutinised for manipulation
approach: Teach one ingredient per post — what it is, what it does, why it's in your formula. This audience buys from whoever educated them, and almost nobody in the tag is actually doing it.
tags: natural skincare, organic, botanical, sensitive skin, balm, soap, cosmetics
